We noticed that we have not been receiving or loading ECOM files for Nike since August 28, 2026.

  • While reviewing the low transaction count for the current date, we observed a significant reduction in overall transactions starting August 28. Further investigation of the logs for the load_raw_ecom_blob.py task confirmed that no c67_rawdata_order files have been loaded since August 28.

  • Last file loaded: prd-datacloud-wus2-ehub-1/c67_rawdata_order/2026/08/27/19/02_42_1.avro
    Pipelines - Run 20260827.2 logs

  • No ECOM files have been loaded after the following run:
    Pipelines - Run 20260828.1 logs

  • We checked with Carl, who confirmed that the services are up and running. However, we are not receiving any data from Nike for the ECOM/RAW_ORDER feed after August 28, 2026.

  • The client has been informed that we have stopped receiving ECOM data from August 28, 2026.

","created":"2026-09-04T15:22:39.337-0400","updated":"2026-09-04T15:22:39.337-0400","updateAuthor":{"accountId":"712020:fc359ce7-3161-48ec-abda-52dd54def66d","displayName":"Akshaya Purappemane"},"jsdPublic":false},{"id":"3327902","author":{"accountId":"712020:688bd119-6d13-450b-95ac-b1ef3fbb547b","displayName":"Juan Martinez"},"body":"

This ticket tracks the same root cause under investigation in RTS-206999. No c67_rawdata_order files have loaded since prd-datacloud-wus2-ehub-1/c67_rawdata_order/2026/08/27/19/02_42_1.avro, confirmed through the load_raw_ecom_blob.py logs referenced in RTS-206999. Carl confirmed on 2026-09-04 that Appriss ingestion services are running.

I reviewed the ARDM load logs for client 067 covering the last successful window, pipeline runs 20260827.2 through 20260828.1. The pipeline completed all SQL transformation steps through Step 20, Loading JSON Table, without a fatal error. One transient 503 occurred during ARDM_13_Tender_Ext.sql at 23:06:22 on 2026-08-28 and the next file executed successfully 39 seconds later. trickle_condition.py reported Vacuum condition not fulfilled, out of time window, and exited cleanly. That message reflects the trickle scheduler stop time logic. It is not an error.

This rules out the ARDM transformation layer as a contributing cause. The gap sits upstream of ARDM, in the raw ECOM ingestion from Nike.

The ARDM Trickle failure in get_exchange_rates.py on 2026-09-02, recovered by L2 on 2026-09-03, is a separate incident. It does not explain the file gap that started four days earlier.

Nike was notified by email on 2026-09-04. Next client follow up is scheduled for 2026-09-08, 08:00 PM IST, per RTS-206999. No action pending on the Appriss side until that follow up or until new files arrive.

Hi @Ayesha Mehar here is the answer for Nike. The text to send them is below the line, ready to go as is.

On what is safe to share: their endpoint and OAuth credential are already theirs from onboarding, so confirming the delivery method adds no exposure. Keep the Event Hub namespace, the hub name, the numeric client ID, blob paths and config keys internal. Those are ours and add nothing for them.

One thing to fix in how the question was framed. Nike assumes we consume a stream on their side. We do not, they publish to us. The consumer client ID they are asking about is their own.

Still open on our side: whether their posts reached our ingestion API after 2026-08-27 19:02 UTC. Event Hub incoming and captured messages are both at zero since then, which rules out anything downstream of the hub. It does not tell us whether their calls were rejected at the API. The API returns 401 resultCode 12 on an OAuth identity mismatch and 400 resultCode 11 on a data type not in the allowed list, and either case looks exactly like this from the hub metrics. I have asked Data Engineering for the inbound logs for that window. That is also why the reply asks Nike for the response codes their side received.

Hello team, here are the five points in order.

  1. Exact stream names. Appriss does not subscribe to a stream on Nike's side. Nike delivers this data by posting it to the Appriss ingestion API, on a separate route per data type. The order feed uses the route provided to your team at onboarding.

  2. Consumer client ID. There is no Appriss consumer client ID for this feed. The credential in use is the OAuth client ID Nike authenticates with when posting to us.

  3. How the data is being consumed. Not a Kafka consumer and not an S3 sink. Your system posts the payload to our ingestion API over HTTPS with OAuth authentication.

  4. Filters being used. None.

  5. Examples of missing data. This is a complete absence of order data, not individual missing events. The last order data reached us on 2026-08-27 at 19:02 UTC and nothing has arrived since. Daily volume before that point ran between 195,352 and 234,363 ECOM transactions.

Two things I need from you. Whether anything changed on your side around 2026-08-27 in the credential or the endpoint used for this feed. And the response codes your system received on its posts after that timestamp.

Thanks @Ayesha Mehar

I have an update regarding this issue. On 2026-09-11, I identified ENG-4235, which involves our Kafka consumer, prd-datacloud-kafka-ingest-wus2, bridging Nike's Kafka topic to our Event Hub for client 067. This shifts the focus of our investigation, as the data gap since 2026-08-27 19:02 UTC may originate on our side rather than Nike's. Consequently, the information previously shared with the client on 2026-09-10 may require correction.

I flagged this to Data Engineering on the same day and am currently awaiting confirmation regarding the consumer's status since that timestamp. I do not have a timeline yet, but I will provide an update as soon as I receive one. Please refrain from contacting Nike until further notice.

@Saddam Hussain
